findings.description: The reserved set includes fixture helpers such as tests/helpers.py, while deletion searches every directory in the grading tree. A valid agent-added src/helpers.py is therefore deleted even though it is an implementation module and cannot cause a pytest test-module collection collision. Package-qualified modules are also removed solely by basename.
findings.failure_mode: Preparation silently removes required solution code, causing import failures or incorrect behavior and grading a correct solution as failing.
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict removal to modules that pytest would actually collect under conflicting import names. Preserve implementation modules, helper modules, and modules with distinct package-qualified names.

findings.description: The preflight assumes every existing Codex auth.json uses ChatGPT JWT credentials. A valid API-key auth.json containing OPENAI_API_KEY and no tokens.access_token now triggers refusal for every non-smoke plan with a Codex-using arm.
findings.failure_mode: Previously usable API-key-authenticated batches cannot start, including dry runs and resumes, because the preflight demands an expiration claim for an authentication mode that has no JWT access token.
findings.suggested_fix: Recognize API-key authentication before checking tokens.access_token and apply the expiration preflight only to authentication modes that use expiring JWT credentials.

findings.description: The reserved-basename set is built from EVERY .py under a fixture directory with a 'tests'/'test' path component (helpers.py, _oracle_x.py, fixtures/data.py, utils.py …) plus every hidden-overlay .py, and the removal walk covers the whole grading tree (src/, package dirs, .venv/, .git/). pytest's 'import file mismatch' only arises for modules pytest imports for collection (python_files: test_*.py / *_test.py, and conftest.py) in rootdir-relative, package-less directories. Nothing else can collide, yet it is deleted. Concrete cases: fixture has tests/utils.py and the agent adds src/app/utils.py -> deleted -> ImportError -> hidden suite fails; a refactor task that legitimately moves tests/test_x.py to tests/unit/test_x.py loses the moved module; an agent-created .venv with site-packages/<pkg>/utils.py loses that file if the fixture has tests/utils.py. The hidden-test path also runs in the AG-35 scenario only because the colliding file happens to be a test; the same code path destroys non-test modules of a correct solution.
findings.failure_mode: A correct agent solution is graded as failing (hidden_tests 0/N or import errors) because a legitimately added or moved module that cannot collide under pytest import rules is unlinked before the test command runs; grade.json reports it only as colliding_tests_removed, so the loss is silent at the row level.
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict `reserved` to basenames pytest actually collects (match python_files patterns: test_*.py / *_test.py; honour pytest.ini/pyproject python_files if present) and never include helper modules. Restrict the walk to the directories the task's test_command targets (or at minimum skip .git, .venv/venv, node_modules, __pycache__). Skip any candidate whose directory chain up to rootdir contains __init__.py (package-qualified modules do not collide in prepend mode). Keep the fixture-path and overlay-path exemptions.

findings.description: `reserved = {d.rsplit('/',1)[-1] for d in owned if d.endswith('.py')}` takes the basename of every hidden-overlay file with no exclusion list. The fixture loop two lines later explicitly excludes __init__.py and conftest.py, and conftest.py is discarded afterwards, but __init__.py from the overlay is not. If any hidden overlay ships tests/hidden/__init__.py (the normal way to make a hidden suite a package so it does not collide with the visible tests), then '__init__.py' is reserved and every __init__.py the agent added anywhere outside the fixture and outside overlay paths — e.g. src/newpkg/__init__.py for a feature-build task that introduces a package — is unlinked.
findings.failure_mode: Agent-created packages become plain directories in the grading tree; imports of them fail (ModuleNotFoundError under default import mode without namespace-package fallback on the test path), and a correct solution is graded as failing with colliding_tests_removed > 0 as the only trace.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the same exclusion to the overlay-derived set: `reserved = {b for b in (d.rsplit('/',1)[-1] for d in owned if d.endswith('.py')) if b not in ('__init__.py','conftest.py')}` (or discard '__init__.py' alongside 'conftest.py' after both sources are merged).

findings.description: The overlay can contain directory entries (the code builds `owned_dirs` from `os.path.isdir(f)` and exempts paths under them), but the reserved-basename set only consults `owned`, i.e. FILE entries. Test modules inside a directory overlay (tests/hidden/ -> tests/hidden/test_slug.py) therefore never enter `reserved`, so an agent-added tests/extra/test_slug.py is kept and the exact collision 1.2.11 claims to fix ('import file mismatch' aborts collection) still occurs for every task whose hidden suite is delivered as a directory overlay. The 1.2.11 header text promises removal for 'a hidden overlay .py file' without this restriction.
findings.failure_mode: For tasks with directory-shaped hidden overlays, pytest aborts collection on the basename clash and a correct solution is graded as failing; grade.json shows colliding_tests_removed: 0, so the operator believes the guard ran.
findings.suggested_fix: When building `reserved`, also os.walk each directory overlay source (`f` where os.path.isdir(f)) and add the basenames of its collected test modules (subject to the DISS-001/DISS-002 exclusions). Alternatively, build `reserved` from the grading tree itself after put_file: every .py under the overlay dests (files and dirs) that pytest would collect.

findings.description: required_until = now + 2 × Σ watchdog_s / concurrency, where watchdog_s is itself already 2 × the phase-sum timeout. For a real batch (8 arms × 16 tasks × 3 trials, watchdog ≈ 2 × 140 min) that is on the order of 1200 h ≈ 50 days; even one arm at concurrency 3 is ≈ 6 days. ChatGPT-auth codex access tokens are short-lived (hours to a few days), so the pre-flight can refuse batches that no `codex login` can satisfy, and the refusal text tells the operator to log in anyway. Note also that pipeline-run.sh copies the host's auth.json afresh at every trial's make_home, so a host-side re-login mid-batch already propagates; the batch-wide horizon is stricter than the mechanism needs.
findings.failure_mode: Non-smoke batches (including --dry-run, since it is not skipped) are refused with 'codex access token expires … before the batch's required horizon …' regardless of how fresh the token is; --resume of an existing batch is refused the same way because the whole recorded plan counts.
findings.suggested_fix: Scale the horizon to what one trial needs plus a margin (e.g. now + max(watchdog_s) × 2, or the expected wall time Σ watchdog / concurrency without the extra 2×), and document that re-running `codex login` on the host mid-batch refreshes later trials because make_home re-copies auth.json per trial. Consider moving the hard check into pipeline-run.sh per trial (exp > now + this trial's watchdog) and keeping the batch-level check as a WARN.

findings.description: A present auth.json whose tokens.access_token is missing or not a three-part JWT is refused outright. The codex CLI also supports API-key auth, where auth.json carries OPENAI_API_KEY (non-null) with auth_mode 'apikey' and no tokens object; such a host is fully functional for the dissent and has no refresh-token hazard (KF-048 is about the ChatGPT refresh flow), yet every non-smoke batch is refused with a 'run codex login' message that would not change the file shape.
findings.failure_mode: Operators using API-key codex auth cannot start or resume any non-smoke batch after this change.
findings.suggested_fix: Before the JWT checks: if data.get('OPENAI_API_KEY') is a non-empty string or data.get('auth_mode') == 'apikey', record checked: false with a reason ('apikey auth, no expiry') and return without refusing.

findings.cross_file_justification: The bats change passes a new `--suite-version` flag to evals/harness/seed-bugfix.sh and seed-refactor.sh (same pattern in seed-refactor.bats line 78). Neither seed script appears in this diff, so unless they already accept that flag the two tests fail at argument parsing.
findings.description: seed-bugfix.bats and seed-refactor.bats now invoke the seed scripts with `--suite-version "$(yq -r .suite_version …)"`. The seed scripts are not touched by this PR. If they do not parse --suite-version, SB-1 and the refactor seed test exit non-zero before producing the 'candidate' line.
findings.failure_mode: Two previously green test cases fail with an unknown-flag usage error; alternatively, if the scripts silently ignore unknown flags, the written suite keeps suite_version 1 and validate-suite rejects it against the suite file's 2, which is the very failure the edit tries to avoid.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm evals/harness/seed-bugfix.sh and seed-refactor.sh accept --suite-version (or add it in this PR, defaulting to the suite file's value so task.yaml and the suite stay consistent without a flag).
